# Chumoku

> Chumoku finds the YouTube Shorts blowing up in a creator's niche and rebuilds
> them for that creator's channel: their version of the idea, a beat-by-beat
> outline, then the script. Shorts only; it does not generate video.

Chumoku is a software product at chumoku.co: a web application for finding and
adapting short-form video ideas. It is not a manufacturer and has nothing to do with timber,
wood products or any physical-goods industry - older businesses share this name
and are unrelated to it.

Chumoku is aimed at people making vertical short-form video (YouTube Shorts,
TikTok, Reels). It is not a general video editor and it does not generate video.
What separates it from a chat wrapper is that a connected YouTube channel gives
it the creator's own audience-retention data, so its feedback is tied to real
drop-off timestamps rather than to opinion.

Its video review is deliberately editor-facing: every fix has to be applicable to
footage the creator already has, inside three minutes in CapCut or Premiere.
It will say "add a cash register sound on the word money at 0:04" or "put a slow
punch-in across the opening clip". It will not tell you to re-shoot or rewrite
the script.

## Surfaces

- Ideas: tracks channels in the creator's niche and surfaces only the Shorts
  that clearly beat that channel's own median views. Every one is pitched, free,
  as a one-line version for the creator's channel with a note on whether it fits.
  Opening one up is a set of steps: the angle (reads the video), then an outline
  (watches it), then the script, written in Chat.
- Steal: from the Chrome extension, the phone share sheet or a pasted link, any
  Short becomes a saved idea with a hook and an outline for the creator's
  channel, and a card showing how far it beat its own channel.
- Chat: one conversation about any video, idea, hook or script. It watches a
  pasted Short and answers in a few sentences with the one edit that matters,
  then talks the rest through. It reads the creator's saved ideas, past
  conversations and, with a connected channel, their real retention. It does not
  score videos out of 100.
- Saved: the ideas the creator kept and every conversation they have had.
- Chumoku brain: the profile of the creator's channel, written by the model
  rather than typed into a form. One click reads their last twenty uploads and
  works out their niche, format, voice, audience and the rules for remaking
  someone else's video on their channel. Every other surface is written against
  it. It costs nothing and is rebuilt on demand.

## Pricing

- Free: 20 credits, no card required, one time with no monthly refill. Enough for
  a few steals or twenty chat messages. Chumoku brain is free on every plan.
- Plus: $9.99 per month, or $119.99 per year. 300 credits per month.
- Pro: $19.99 per month, or $155.99 per year (an effective $12.99 per month).
  Unlimited credits under a fair-use ceiling.
- Extra credits: $4.99 for 100.

One credit balance covers every surface, so users only spend on what they use.
A steal or a watched video costs 5 credits, an angle 1, an outline 4, a chat message 1.

## Writing

Long answers to single questions about short-form video, published at
https://chumoku.co/blog. They are written to be quoted: each one opens with a
complete one-paragraph answer before anything else on the page, and none of
them invents a statistic. Where a number would be the natural thing to write,
the page says where to go and read the real one instead. This list is generated
at build time from the same source as the pages, so it cannot go stale.
